discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 111025
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
525 AM EST Wed Nov 11 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Rain showers develop and spread across the area this afternoon
  and early evening. An isolated thunderstorm possible portions
  of northwest Indiana this afternoon and early evening with
  isolated wind gusts of over 40 mph possible with any showers
  or isolated storms.

- Lake effect showers impact areas mainly west of US-31 in
  northwest Indiana and far southwest Lower Michigan Thursday
  through Friday night. Snow is expected to mix in by late 
  Thursday night into Friday morning. Additional lake effect 
  snow showers are possible early Saturday. Some slushy snow 
  accumulations are possible with the lake effect, mainly early 
  Friday morning across northwest Indiana. 

- Below normal temperatures Thursday through this weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 340 AM EST Wed Nov 11 2026

Water vapor imagery early this morning depicts a sharp upper level 
short wave across western Iowa. An eastern Pacific jet streak 
progressing through the base of this trough will induce sfc 
cyclogenesis across southeast Iowa/west central Illinois this 
morning into this afternoon as sfc reflection reaches east central 
Indiana by this evening. Low level winds will back this afternoon in 
advance of this trough and strengthening low level flow in this 
deepening phase will allow for northward push to low/mid level theta-
e boundary currently displaced to the south-southwest of the local 
area. Given strongly forced nature to this setup and respectable low-
mid level RH developing, have maintained likely rain shower PoPs 
from west to east this afternoon into this evening. While there is a 
period of stronger advection this afternoon, the short duration of 
this advection will make it difficult to realize any appreciable 
instability. Moistening low and mid levels combined with maintenance 
of some drier sub-cloud air could provide some favorable 
theta-e differentials for a period of gusty winds associated 
with the showers (perhaps SPS level gusts over 40 mph) late this
afternoon into early this evening. Maturing nature to low level
baroclinic zone and sharpness of low/mid level trough may 
support a deformation- band of rain into this evening. Otherwise
today, the warm advection regime will provide above normal 
temperatures despite the increased cloud over with highs from 
the mid 50s north to low to mid 60s south. 

Passage of the initial upper trough this evening will set the stage 
for favorable storm track for several additional disturbances in 
northerly upper flow to bring reinforcing shots of cold air 
into the southern Great Lakes region later tonight into Friday. 
Lake effect rain showers are expected to start as early as later
this evening as shallow lake induced instability develops. 
Initially this lake effect may manifest as cellular convective 
mode given some synoptic low level troughing expected across the
southern Great Lakes and shallow nature to instability depth. 
The more impressive synoptic trough will dive south across the 
southern Great Lakes on Thursday, with a period of isolated to 
scattered rain showers area-wide as this trough drops south. In 
the wake of this disturbance, flow profiles should begin to 
align more favorably down long-axis of Lake Michigan for a more 
dominant single band event Thursday night into Friday. Lake 
temperatures remain above normal, generally in the 80-90 
percentile for mid November. While this will aid in lake induced
instability, it does also raise questions of low level thermal 
modification downwind of Lake Michigan and influences on precip 
types. Have generally followed idea of most of higher-res 
guidance in greater potential of snow overnight a bit away from 
the lakeshore where this modification of low level thermals will
not be as dramatic. After 06Z Thursday night, depth of cold air
should overcome marginal low level wet bulbs for a period of 
mainly snow shower ptypes especially away from the lakeshore. 
There are also some indications that another synoptic mid/upper 
trough could be rotating cyclonically across the western Great 
Lakes which could provide some increased lift to nudge areas to 
snow ptype for a brief window closer to the lakeshore also. Of 
course, plenty of uncertainties as to exact low level flow 
trajectories and timing of this mid level short waves, but 
confidence is increasing in the potential of some localized 
inland slushy accumulations of an inch or two across portions of
NW Indiana and possibly far SW Lower Michigan early Friday 
morning. 

Loss of stronger synoptic forcing during the day Thursday combined 
with diurnal tendencies should take p-types back to rain during the 
day as low level flow trajectories remain favorable for an extended 
period of lake effect precipitation. Another upper level spoke to 
the broad upper level negative height anomaly is progged to dive 
south to the southern Great Lakes Friday night into early Saturday. 
Low level gradient will be a bit weaker by this time which could 
support some land breeze sharpening of lake effect banding. The main 
question for Friday night/Saturday AM will be potential of enough 
low level airmass modification to keep p-types as mainly rain.
One wildcard will be if stronger low level lift induced by 
stronger convergence with possible land breeze enhancement can 
be enough to changeover precip types for a time. Depth of lake 
induced instability does appear to start to diminish during the
overnight hours Friday night. There is also some question as to
whether favored area of banding may shift west of the local 
area briefly Friday night in response to the stronger synoptic 
forcing.

Lake effect rain showers continue Saturday but should be in a 
diminishing state Saturday afternoon as inversion heights
continue to crash with the approach of the low level ridge 
axis. Thermal advections will be weak through the weekend which 
will keep below normal temperatures in place. The longwave 
ridging across central CONUS should begin to shift off to the 
east middle of next week which will allow some moderation of 
temperatures and potentially some additional rain chances in the
Day 7 to 9 period.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z THURSDAY/...
Issued at 524 AM EST Wed Nov 11 2026

VFR outside of some early morning patchy fog through mid afternoon.
A frontal zone and developing sfc reflection then drop through 
KSBN late this afternoon/early this evening, and KFWA this evening
with showers and northerly winds up to near 12 knots (briefly
gusting 20 knots plus) along and behind. Ceilings drop into the
low VFR or high MVFR category during this time.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory from 7 PM this evening to 7 PM EST Friday 
     for LMZ043-046.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Marsili
AVIATION...Steinwedel

spc.summary: Thunderstorms capable of isolated large hail, damaging wind gusts, and perhaps a tornado will be possible Wednesday afternoon and evening across parts of the Ohio and western Tennessee Valleys.
spc.text:
SPC AC 110551

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1151 PM CST Tue Nov 10 2026

   Valid 111200Z - 121200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
   THE OHIO AND WESTERN TENNESSEE VALLEYS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms capable of isolated large hail, damaging wind gusts,
   and perhaps a tornado will be possible Wednesday afternoon and
   evening across parts of the Ohio and western Tennessee Valleys.

   ...Synopsis...

   A lead short-wave trough will move through portions of the southern
   Great Lakes and OH Valley on Wednesday, ahead of a stronger upstream
   system and attending mid/upper-level wind maxima, which will
   progress through the mid-MO and mid-MS Valleys into the Mid-South/TN
   Valley. The net result will be a broad zone of height falls/forcing
   for ascent overspreading the OH and TN Valleys Wednesday afternoon
   into night. In the low levels, a cyclone will track from eastern IA
   at 12Z Wednesday through central IL and IN during the afternoon
   before reaching the upper OH Valley late Wednesday night. Meanwhile,
   a trailing cold front will advance southeast through the mid-MS,
   much of the OH, and TN Valleys during the forecast period.


   ...Ohio Valley into the Mid-South and Tennessee Valley...

   00Z observed soundings and current surface observations indicate the
   presence of a partially modified continental-polar air mass in place
   over the southern Plains into Ozark Plateau, characterized by
   boundary-layer dewpoints in the 50s and lowest 100-mb mean-mixing
   ratios of 9-10.5 g/kg. That moisture will be advected into the
   region on Wednesday ahead of the front and beneath a plume of
   modestly steep mid-level lapse rates (e.g., 7-7.5 C/km), yielding a
   relatively narrow axis of MLCAPE of 750-1250 J/kg by mid-late
   afternoon.

   Divergence aloft in the exit region of the upper-level jet streak
   will enhance convergence in the vicinity of the surface low and
   trailing front, resulting in a gradual increase in storm coverage
   and intensity through the afternoon, initially from northern and
   eastern IL into IN. Subsequent storm development is anticipated by
   late afternoon into evening from portions of western and central KY
   into middle TN, though storm coverage is likely to decrease with
   southward extent.

   The presence of 35-40 kt of effective bulk shear with a vector
   orientation largely perpendicular to the surface front should favor
   semi-discrete storm modes, which is consistent with several REFS
   ensemble members. The somewhat marginal CAPE-shear parameter space
   may limit the potential for sustained supercells, and an associated
   greater severe weather threat. Nonetheless, the relatively steep
   low/midlevel lapse rates with 500-mb temperatures approaching -20 C
   will be supportive of isolated occurrences of large hail and
   damaging winds, especially with any transient supercell structures
   and/or bowing line segment. A tornado is possible during the late
   afternoon or early evening as low-level shear strengthens. However,
   convective inhibition is expected to increase fairly quickly during
   the evening, suggesting any threat will be short-lived.  


   ...Central and Southern Florida...

   A moist and moderately unstable air mass (e.g., MLCAPE of 1000-1500
   J/kg) is forecast to the south of a weak west-to-east oriented
   surface boundary/confluence zone over the central peninsula. Aided
   by the glancing influence of a weak disturbance passing to the
   north, thunderstorms should increase in areal coverage through the
   afternoon, especially from the south-central peninsula toward the
   Atlantic Coast. The presence of 35-40 kt of deep-layer shear may
   foster a few stronger storms capable of hail and/or outflow winds
   approaching severe levels.

   ..Mead.. 11/11/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 110641

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1241 AM CST Wed Nov 11 2026

   Valid 121200Z - 131200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   No severe thunderstorms are forecast across the U.S. Thursday and
   Thursday night.

   ...DISCUSSION...
   An upper-level trough will move across the eastern U.S. on Thursday.
   Ahead of the trough, isolated thunderstorms will be possible in the
   morning and afternoon across parts of the Mid-Atlantic and far
   southern New England southward to near Cape Hatteras. Additional
   storms may form within a moist airmass over south Florida and along
   the immediate coast of southern California ahead of an approaching
   upper-level trough. No severe threat is forecast across the
   continental U.S. Thursday and Thursday night.

   ..Broyles.. 11/11/2026

SPC AC 110827

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0227 AM CST Wed Nov 11 2026

   Valid 131200Z - 141200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   No severe thunderstorms are forecast across the U.S. Friday and
   Friday night.

   ...DISCUSSION...
   An upper-level trough will move eastward across the Atlantic Coastal
   states Friday into Friday night, as a shortwave mid-level ridge
   moves into the High Plains. Further west, an upper-level trough will
   move onshore into the western U.S. on Friday. Thunderstorms will be
   possible ahead of this feature in parts of the Desert Southwest and
   near the trough along the coasts of northern California and
   southwest Oregon. No severe threat is forecast across the
   continental U.S. Friday and Friday night.

   ..Broyles.. 11/11/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
